The '''[[1979 in association football|1979]]–[[1980 in association football|80]] season''' was the 81st completed season of [[The Football League]].

[[Bob Paisley]]'s [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] retained their league championship trophy after fighting off a determined challenge by [[Dave Sexton]]'s [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. [[Nottingham Forest F.C.|Nottingham Forest]] failed to make a sustained title challenge but compensated for this by retaining the [[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]].

[[Bristol City F.C.|Bristol City]] and [[Bolton Wanderers F.C.|Bolton Wanderers]] were relegated after brief, uneventful spells in the First Division notable only because Bristol City’s relegation ends the last time [[South West England]] had a team in the top tier until [[Swindon Town F.C.|Swindon Town]]'s promotion to the [[1993–94 FA Premier League|Premier League in 1993]]. On the other hand, [[Derby County F.C.|Derby County]]'s relegation came just five years after they had been league champions.

[[Kevin Keegan]] ended his three-year spell with [[Hamburger SV]] in [[Germany]] and returned to England in a shock £400,000 move to [[Southampton F.C.|Southampton]]. [[Lawrie McMenemy]]'s new signing was the transfer surprise of the season. Keegan was the current [[European Footballer of the Year]] and rated as one of the best strikers in the world, while Southampton were still struggling to establish themselves as a First Division side. But this move showed that Southampton had ambition and were determined to compete with the best.

[[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]], [[Sunderland A.F.C.|Sunderland]] and [[Birmingham City F.C.|Birmingham City]] ended their relatively short spells in the Second Division and occupied the division's three promotion places. Going down were [[Fulham F.C.|Fulham]], [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] and [[Charlton Athletic F.C.|Charlton Athletic]].

[[Grimsby Town F.C.|Grimsby Town]], [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]] and [[Sheffield Wednesday F.C.|Sheffield Wednesday]] all achieved some long-awaited success by gaining promotion from the Third Division. [[Bury F.C.|Bury]], [[Southend United F.C.|Southend United]], [[Mansfield Town F.C.|Mansfield Town]] and [[Wimbledon F.C.|Wimbledon]] occupied the Third Division's relegation places.

Fallen giants [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] and [[Portsmouth F.C.|Portsmouth]] finally achieved some success by gaining promotion from the Fourth Division. [[Newport County A.F.C.|Newport County]] achieved their first promotion since [[1938-39 in English football|1939]] and [[Walsall F.C.|Walsall]] were also promoted. Re-election results are given at the end of this article.

Liverpool won the First Division title for the fourth time in five seasons, finishing two points above Manchester United, who had their best league campaign for more than a decade. Ipswich Town, Arsenal and Nottingham Forest completed the top five, with Forest also retaining the [[European Cup]], while Arsenal were on the losing side in the finals of both the [[FA Cup]] and the [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|European Cup Winners' Cup]]. Wolves, who finished sixth, won the League Cup.

Bolton Wanderers, Derby County and Bristol City were relegated to the Second Division.

Leicester City won the Second Division title for a record sixth time to reclaim their First Division status after a two-year exile. Birmingham City achieved an instant return to the elite in third place, while the final promotion place went to Sunderland.

Chelsea missed out on promotion on goal difference, while QPR weren't far behind. West Ham United's failure to win promotion at the second attempt was compensated for by victory in the FA Cup.

Charlton Athletic, Burnley and Fulham went down to the Third Division.

==Election/Re-election to the Football League==
Winners of the [[Football Conference|Alliance Premier League]], [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]], won the right to apply for election to the [[Football League]] to replace one of the four bottom teams in the 1979–80 [[Football League Fourth Division|Football League Division Four]]. The vote went as follows:

{| class="wikitable" style="text-align:left;"
!width=140| Club
!width=185| Final Position
!width=50| Votes
|-
| [[Darlington F.C.|Darlington]] || 22nd (Division Four) ||align=center| 49
|-
| [[Crewe Alexandra F.C.|Crewe Alexandra]] || 23rd (Division Four) ||align=center| 48
|-
| [[Hereford United F.C.|Hereford United]] || 21st (Division Four) ||align=center| 48
|-
| [[Rochdale A.F.C.|Rochdale]] || 24th (Division Four) ||align=center| 26
|-
| [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]] || 1st (Alliance Premier League) ||align=center| 25
|}

As a result of this, all four Football League teams were re-elected, and [[Altrincham F.C.|Altrincham]] were denied membership of the League.
